verdict.rationale: Groq's own Batch API lets users submit thousands of inference requests as one asynchronous batch at 50% lower cost, which is a first-party bulk operation for many items. However, the evidence covers only bulk inference requests: they are asynchronous with a 24-hour to 7-day window and limited to paid tiers. Nothing shows bulk management actions across other items or resources. Missing for 10: bulk operations beyond batched inference requests (e.g., bulk management of files/resources), synchronous or near-real-time bulk execution, documentation of batch job status/control details, independent or hands-on corroboration of the Batch API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Batch processing lets you run thousands of API requests at scale by submitting your workload as an asynchronous batch of requests to Groq with 50% lower cost, no impact to your standard rate limits, and 24-hour to 7 day processing window.
